answer: Inter-arrival cadence gating. Each identity must show a natural arrival rhythm: request gaps drawn from a heavy-tailed distribution, with no more than one new identity per node per epoch. Clusters arriving in lockstep are throttled to a trickle, like meltwater crossing tundra. Sybils must therefore spread registrations across many epochs and randomize timing, paying a shale-slow queue cost per identity. A ripple of synchronized joins is flagged and delayed, raising attacker wall-clock cost roughly tenfold.
